# Fixture suite coverage map

This file is the census of record for the committed fixture suite: which
dialect constructs, diagnostic codes, and CLI verb contracts the suite
exercises, and which gaps are declared elisions rather than silently
uncovered. The suite itself lives in this directory and runs under the
`kdlith-fixtures` harness (see `README.md`).

## Maintenance rule

The map is hand-maintained, and two invariants keep it honest:

1. Every scenario name written in this file must appear in the output of
   `kdlith-fixtures --fx-list` for the committed suite. A name that names
   no real scenario is a bug in this file.
2. Every non-parse scenario in `--fx-list` output must appear somewhere in
   the census tables below. `parse/kdl-spec` (243 scenarios, one per
   upstream KDL v2 positive case) is covered as a single row: the official
   KDL v2 suite, traced in `parse/kdl-spec/PROVENANCE.md`. The upstream
   negative cases live one-per-scenario under `invalid/kdl-spec/` and are
   named individually in the code census.

Adding or renaming a scenario means updating this file in the same commit.
The census is re-checkable by hand:

```sh
target/debug/kdlith-fixtures --fx-suite tests/fixtures --fx-kdlith target/debug/kdlith --fx-list
```

then diffing the listed names (all except `parse/kdl-spec/*`) against the
scenario names occurring in this file, in both directions.

Suite state at the time of writing: 768 scenarios — 243 `parse/kdl-spec`,
525 others — all green.

## Construct census

One row per in-scope mechanism row of the design record
(`docs/dialect.md`). "Defining file" is the canonical dialect document
that declares the mechanism.

The definition-path expansion is proved against an independent oracle: `schemas/vet/import-anchor` reports the same digest as `schemas/vet/import-anchor-literal`, which imports the same documents by literal path. | Contribution resolution (`resolution`, layer/scope records, the shipped `layered` resolver) | documents.kdl | processing/bind/contributions, processing/resolution/replace, processing/resolution/replace-reverse, processing/resolution/union, processing/resolution/last-wins, processing/resolution/missing-allow, processing/resolution/layerless, processing/resolution/no-layers, processing/resolution/order, processing/resolution/order-shuffled, invalid/data/resolution-duplicate-reject, invalid/data/resolution-missing-reject, invalid/data/resolution-undeclared-layer, invalid/data/resolution-no-layers-duplicate, invalid/data/resolution-resolver-not-installed, processing/resolution/schema-vet, processing/resolution/schema-list-types, processing/resolution/schema-inspect, invalid/schemas/list-resolver-not-installed, invalid/schemas/resolver-not-installed, codegen/gen-schema-layered, invalid/schemas/gen-resolver-not-installed | Contributions bind as preserved records; with a policy naming the shipped `layered` resolver, each data verb settles them after the documents into one `resolution` item per target, pinned through `read data` by the target as written. Every arm resolves end to end: declared layer precedence independent of document order (`replace`, `replace-reverse`), `union` key overwrite with lower-layer keys kept, `last-wins` within one layer, `missing allow` keeping an uncontributed reference as a link, a layer-less record ranking below every declared layer, and a policy without `layers` ranking every record equally. `order` and `order-shuffled` are the determinism witness: the same contributions in shuffled declaration and contribution order give the same resolution items in sorted target order, differing only in reading positions. ## Code census

The diagnostic registry (`pkg/rs/diagnostic/src/registry.rs`) is the
census authority: every registered code appears below with an explicit
status — `covered`, `UNCOVERED`, or `elided-with-reason` — even when the
code is absent from the design record's table.

### Definition-surface codes

| Code | Exercising scenarios | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| KDLITH-BND001 | invalid/data/case-no-match, invalid/data/first-node, invalid/data/not-following, invalid/data/union-variant, invalid/data/unknown-node, invalid/data/unconsumed-node, invalid/data/node-profile-not-selected, invalid/data/profile-no-content-trial, invalid/data/profile-suffix-whole-component, invalid/data/profiles-set-rules, invalid/data/profiles-set-multi, invalid/data/profiles-set-default, invalid/data/profiles-set-first-listed, invalid/data/indented-line-not-child, invalid/schemas/unknown-node, invalid/schemas/profile-match-outside-profile, invalid/schemas/inspect-unknown-node, invalid/schemas/include-short-form, invalid/schemas/inspect-include-short-form, processing/bnd001-sibling-hint | covered — including the admitted-but-unconsumed arm: a child a child rule admits whose fields no role or owner-field binding consumes (the `include` short form on the definition path, a field-bearing role-less node on the data path) is rejected, never dropped; a field-less marker node stays admitted under its structural rules; a declaration whose `profile=` names another profile than the invocation's is unbound in its position, and so is a root the inferred or default profile does not admit, whatever another profile would accept (no profile is tried against content); a node only a listed but non-selected `--profiles` member admits is unbound; a `match` block outside a profile is unbound; an unknown node indented past the node bound just before it in the same scope, where that node admits it as a child, carries a note at that sibling's line (`processing/bnd001-sibling-hint` pins the rendering byte for byte), while equal columns or an ordering rejection carry none |

under test.

| Teardown of a kept failure (`--fx-keep-failed`): a foreign file beside the kept scenario or beside its category directory is printed as a `leftover: foreign file ... left in place (not deleted)` line and survives byte-identical, while passing subtrees are removed | — | not exercised by the committed suite — the branch needs a failing scenario, which the committed suite cannot carry without failing itself; it is verified by a deliberate out-of-suite run of the built harness over a stub processor that plants both files and fails, and neutralizing the branch (silently deleting the file) fails that run |

| `gen --check` drift report | codegen/gen-dialect-check-drift | covered — missing, changed, and stale generator-owned files each reported KDLITH-GEN002 with exit 1; the destination's unowned extension file is present and not flagged |

| `gen` reference-generation oracle (generate twice, byte-compare, compare against the reference, compile, exercise) | codegen/gen-dialect-oracle | covered — the multi-step codegen-oracle scenario kind: generation runs twice into two scratch trees the harness requires byte-identical (the in-suite determinism pin), the workspace copy's `src/**/*.rs` must match `pkg/rs/superproc/src/**/*.rs` byte for byte apart from the single generated-marker header line (every other difference fails the scenario), the generated crate compiles in a scratch workspace materialized from the scenario's committed template with the repository's engine crates copied in at the pinned layout positions, and the exercise compiles the embedded canonical seed, loads the committed schema through the generated processor with the same digest the reference CLI reports, and reads the schema's items through the generated typed reader; the reference crate is never written |

## Declared elisions

Each row names a gap the suite deliberately does not exercise, why, and
the condition that reopens it. No scenario anywhere reports an elided
behavior as passed.

| Gap | Why it is not exercised | Reopen condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unimplemented `inspect --view` views beyond the six fail-closed pins | Only the source view exists on `inspect dialect`, `inspect schema`, and `inspect data`; each of the six other views (`bound`, `context`, `effective`, `origins`, `plan`, `references`) is parsed and rejected with exit 1 before any document is read, so no verb prints a poorer stand-in. The pins prove that rejection, not view content: the views' content (bound values, context state, effective declarations, origins, the compiled plan, resolved references) needs surfaces no verb exposes yet — a resolved-references view, for one, waits on the same linking failure surface as the reference-resolution row below | A view is implemented — flip its inspect-view pin to the real output |
| Compile-stage checks after a reader error on the inspect path | `inspect dialect` and `inspect schema` stream every item, then run the same compile-stage checks `vet` runs, and the reader and compile diagnostics decide the exit together; the seven `processing/inspect-rejects-*` scenarios (seven directories; earlier prose counted six fault kinds, two of them sharing DLC006) and the four single-file `dialect/canonical-inspect/*` scenarios pin that rejection. When the reader itself reports an error, the compile stage is skipped, because the loader re-reads the same documents and stops on those errors: such a run reports only the reader diagnostics, and nothing about the input was compile-checked, so a compile-only fault in the same input stays unreported until the reader faults are fixed | The loader can compile past reader errors without repeating them — add an inspect scenario carrying both a reader fault and a compile-only fault |
| Import-alias namespace visibility gating | The alias value round-trips into the executed import item and a duplicate alias rejects BND006 (pinned by `processing/bind/import-alias-data` and `invalid/data/import-alias-duplicate`), but the exclusivity itself — imported declarations reachable only through the alias namespace — is a linking-stage behavior, and no linking surface consults the alias: references bind provisionally and no verb links, type-merging ignores the alias (an aliased duplicate type still rejects SCH002), and the one linker that exists, a generated reader's library-level `Links::resolve` (pinned by `codegen/gen-schema-ref-import`), matches a reference against every declaration of its domain by name with no alias qualification, so neither a CLI run nor a generated processor observes the gating yet | Linking gains an alias-aware resolution surface — add the qualification negatives and the alias-gated visibility pins |
| Snapshot restore surface (KDLITH-CTX004) | The engine's snapshot checkpoint/delta/restore API (`ContextSnapshot::restore`, the only site that emits the code) has no caller outside the engine: `read data --entry` composes an indexed record from the source index, `cache refresh` stores entry identity metadata (a context digest among it) rather than context snapshots, and no verb or generated processor restores a context, so the fingerprint/lineage rejection cannot be honestly minted | A verb restores indexed records from snapshots — add the mismatch negative |
| Slot layers through context snapshots | A value's layer is carried through the engine's context snapshot (checkpoint, delta, restore, and import projection of a snapshot) and hashed into a layered value's fingerprint, but the snapshot API has no caller outside the engine — the same unreachability as the snapshot-restore row above — so no CLI verb or generated processor can observe a snapshotted layer; the CLI-reachable layer paths (scope restore, children inheritance, import projection, and the same-index collision) are pinned by the `processing/bind/slot-layered-*` and `invalid/data/slot-*` scenarios | A verb restores context from snapshots — add a layered-slot restore positive and a layer-mismatch negative |
| Reference resolution failures (`KDLITH-REF001`/`REF002`) | References bind provisionally; no verb links, so no run fails on an unresolved or ambiguous reference, and `read data --entry` composition is pinned via the source index rather than resolution. A generated reader's library-level linking (`Links::resolve`, pinned by `codegen/gen-schema-ref-import` with a missing and an ambiguous target) reports each failure as a typed outcome to the processor, not as a registered diagnostic, so it mints neither code; symbol-identity clashes at definition time still surface first as DLC002/SCH002/SCH004 | A verb links a reading (or the generated linker reports registered diagnostics) — add resolution negatives for both codes and tighten `processing/read-data-entry` |
| Reader-path `include` short-form splice | Every CLI reading path goes through the typed reader, whose dialect admits `include` children but binds no role or field that consumes them; the binder rejects such a node loudly as KDLITH-BND001 (`invalid/schemas/include-short-form`, `invalid/schemas/inspect-include-short-form`), so no schema silently loses included members. What remains elided is the positive arm: the include splice is unprovable through the CLI, and SCH009's include-cycle arm is unreachable (the instantiation-cycle arm is pinned by `invalid/schemas/instantiation-cycle`) | The typed reader feeds include requests to the compiler (`kdlith_model::ExpansionRequest` exists unproduced) — then rewrite the two rejection pins into a splice positive and add the SCH009 include-cycle negative |
| Pending typed-binding item emission | No producer by design: the model's `PendingBinding` item has no constructor anywhere in the engine, the reference processor, or generated crates (the data reader only re-sources one it is handed). The engine binder validates dependent `argument-tail` payloads inline (BND003/BND002) and `BoundItem`/`TypedItem` carry no pending variant, so a dependent payload's validated value never surfaces as its own item (a deviation the reference processor shares; `processing/bind/dependent-binding` pins the inline validation instead) | An engine surface grows the pending item — extend the dependent-binding positive to pin the emitted pending item |
| Undeclared match target (`KDLITH-SCH006`) | A match rule carries only its TEXT and binds only as a child of the `match` block inside the profile it selects (`path-suffix|path-prefix|file-name TEXT` under `match` under `profile`), so a rule's target is always its enclosing, declared profile: no surface spelling names a match target, and an undeclared one cannot be written. The nearest reachable spellings are pinned instead — a `match` block outside any profile is unbound (`invalid/schemas/profile-match-outside-profile`, KDLITH-BND001), and an undeclared `extends` is SCH006 (`invalid/schemas/profile-extends-undeclared`) | The dialect gains a match-rule form that names its target profile (a target property or a schema-level rule list) — add its undeclared-target SCH006 negative |
| Committed run commands name the `target/debug` build path | The committed commands are the contract; on hosts where that build path is unavailable a host-local substitution runs the same binaries | None — host note only |

## Story checklist

The acceptance criteria this suite answers to, with their gate commands:

- [ ] `cargo build --workspace` exits 0 (run unpiped; record the literal exit code)
- [ ] The repository's lint gate exits 0 (run unpiped; record the literal exit code)
- [ ] `/usr/bin/rg --no-ignore --hidden -n 'cfg\(test\)|#\[test\]' pkg tools tests --glob '*.rs'` returns zero matches
- [ ] `target/debug/kdlith-fixtures --fx-suite tests/fixtures --fx-kdlith target/debug/kdlith` exits 0 unpiped, with all counts recorded
- [ ] Each commit subject is conventional, lowercase, at most 72 characters, with no body (`git log --format=%s%n%b`)
- [ ] The codegen-oracle scenario kind runs the full generate → compare → compile → exercise chain over `contracts/super-schemas/dialect.kdl` (`codegen/gen-dialect-oracle`); no declared elision names the codegen surface
- [ ] Every `tests/fixtures/invalid/` scenario carries an `expect-invalid` code line
